draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Talakadu! This town on the Kaveri once had over 30 temples, and most of them now lie buried under the sand.
draft.hungryLine: My notes don't list eateries here, so carry water and snacks for your walk among the temples.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Group of temples at Talakadu is just a 5 min walk, where the river bends and the sand spreads wide along its banks.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit by the Kaveri where it changes course and the sand stretches out. It's the setting that gives Talakadu its strange beauty.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Excavations in the sand dunes here have turned up several ruined temples from the Western Ganga dynasty.

spots.name: Group of temples at Talakadu
spots.detail: 5 min walk · Ganga, Chola and Hoysala temples in the sand

legends.title: Tala and Kadu
legends.body: Tradition says twin brothers named Tala and Kadu cut down a tree that wild elephants worshipped, and found an image of Shiva inside. Two stone images said to be the brothers stand in front of the Veerabadra swamy temple.

tips.title: Be ready for sand.
tips.body: Sand covers a wide area around the temples, so wear footwear that's easy to walk in and slip off.

tips.title: Dress for a pilgrimage site.
tips.body: The temples are a popular Hindu pilgrimage site, so dress modestly.

story.title: Lost in time
story.body: The town's origin is lost in antiquity, and tradition names it after the twin brothers Tala and Kadu.

story.title: Ganga temples
story.body: Several temples were built here under the Western Ganga dynasty, many now ruined under the dunes.

story.title: Two that survived
story.body: The Pataleshvara and Maraleshvara temples, from the reign of Rachamalla Satyavakya IV, are still intact.

story.title: A victory temple
story.body: Hoysala King Vishnuvardhana built the Kirtinarayana temple in 1117 to celebrate beating the Cholas at Talakad.

story.title: Pilgrims and sand
story.body: The surviving temples, where the Kaveri changes course, draw Hindu pilgrims, and the Vaidyeshvara is the largest and most ornate.
